name: Marketing, creative and digital agencies

problems.words: Clients send briefs on WhatsApp voice notes and details get lost
quick_ideas: Have the account manager write each new brief back to the client once for confirmation, so both sides agree what was asked
Keep this week's briefs in one shared place, so designers aren't digging through chats.

workzap_build.text: brief intake that turns a client request into a structured task with deadline and assets, confirmed back to the client automatically.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many active clients is the team handling?
problems.free_stops: the intake fields and confirmation flow are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many brief details were missing from this week's voice notes, so you see where work gets delayed.
Give one person the job of writing every new brief in one notebook, so designers work from one agreed version.

problems.words: Approvals take forever, then they want everything live tomorrow
quick_ideas: Put an approval-needed-by date on everything you send this week, so delays are visible
List what is waiting on clients today, so the AMs know who to chase.

workzap_build.text: an approval tracker per deliverable with automatic client reminders and a daily list of what's stuck and for how long.

problems.free_stops: reminder timings and escalation are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every job waiting on approval at today's close, so tomorrow's rush requests are easier to challenge with facts.
Give one account manager the daily handover list of pending approvals, so chasing does not get missed between shifts.

problems.words: Unlimited revisions are killing my designers
quick_ideas: Count revision rounds on this week's deliverables, so you see where the extra work goes
Share that count with your heaviest client once, so the conversation is based on facts.

workzap_build.text: every deliverable tracked with revision rounds counted against what the agreement allows, flagged when it goes over.

problems.free_stops: how rounds are counted and flagged is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which deliverables came back most often this week, so you see where unlimited revisions are draining designers.
Give one person the job of noting every revision round in one list, so repeat rework stops slipping by unnoticed.

problems.words: Retainers keep growing in work but not in fee
quick_ideas: Write down once what each retainer includes per month, so drift is easy to spot
Compare last month's delivery against it for your two biggest clients, so you know where to start.

workzap_build.text: a retainer scope register comparing what's included with what was delivered each month, flagging overruns as they happen.

problems.free_stops: how scope is defined and compared is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare what each retainer promised with what your team actually delivered this week, so scope creep has a clear shape.
Give one person one notebook for out of scope requests, so extra work on retainers stops getting absorbed quietly.

problems.words: I genuinely don't know which clients make us money
quick_ideas: Ask the team to note time per client for one month, so you get a first real comparison
Put that next to each retainer fee once, so the loss-makers show up.

workzap_build.text: light time logging per client and service, rolled up daily into profitability by client.

problems.free_stops: how time is logged without slowing the team is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write each client's fee beside this week's team time notes, so the weakest client economics stand out quickly.
Give one person the job of collecting daily time notes in one place, so client effort is no longer guessed.

problems.words: We front ad spend on our cards and get reimbursed late
quick_ideas: List every client's outstanding ad spend once, so the size of the gap is clear
Raise the largest one with that client this week, so reimbursement starts moving.

workzap_build.text: an ad spend reimbursement tracker per client with invoices, ageing and reminders.

problems.free_stops: the reimbursement and reminder flow is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: List each client with unreimbursed ad spend beside the oldest waiting item, so the cash strain is clear at a glance.
Give one person one list for reimbursement follow ups, so client chasing happens on time every week.

problems.words: Monthly reports to clients take two days to build manually
quick_ideas: Pick one report layout for all clients, so the team stops rebuilding from scratch
Note which numbers clients actually read, so you can cut the rest.

workzap_build.text: monthly client reports pulled automatically from the ad platforms and social analytics into a branded summary.

problems.free_stops: which sources are connected and the report design are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark which report sections clients actually discuss on calls this month, so the team sees what is worth building.
Give one person one master report checklist, so monthly reporting stops being rebuilt differently each time.

problems.words: Posts get missed because the calendar wasn't updated
quick_ideas: Check next week's content calendar against what's actually ready, so gaps are caught now
Name one owner per client calendar, so updates aren't left to chance.

workzap_build.text: a shared content calendar with status for every post from drafted to live, alerting the owner when a scheduled post isn't approved in time.

problems.free_stops: the status stages and alerts are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's scheduled posts with what actually went live, so missed updates on the calendar show up clearly.
Give one person the end of day calendar check, so missed posts stop slipping through stale schedules.

problems.words: Designers are overloaded one week and idle the next
quick_ideas: Put every designer's tasks for the next two weeks on one board, so overloads show
Move one task from the busiest person, so the team feels the change.

workzap_build.text: a team capacity board by person and week that updates as tasks are assigned.

problems.free_stops: how workload is measured per person is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each designer's waiting work at today's close, so uneven loading across the team is obvious this week.
Give one person the daily job of balancing incoming design tasks, so busy and idle weeks get smoothed earlier.

problems.words: Clients leave after three months and we don't know why
quick_ideas: Ask your last few departed clients one polite question about why, so you get real reasons
Book a check-in call with each newer client, so problems surface early.

workzap_build.text: a client health view combining approvals, revisions, response times and payment behaviour to flag at-risk clients.

problems.free_stops: the health signals and thresholds are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note why each client left after three months on one page, so patterns behind churn stop feeling random.
Give one person a weekly client health check list, so early warning signs get acted on before exits.

never_say: That ads, posts or campaigns will deliver any result, ROAS or follower count.
Anything about fake reviews, bought followers, deceptive ads, scraping personal data or using content without rights.
Marketing strategy, legal or tax advice.
Requests for ad account logins, passwords, card details or client customer lists.

sample_reply.person: Revisions are my biggest headache. Clients send changes late at night and the designers redo work again and again. What can I do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there's a way to get this under control, starting this week. 1) Count the revision rounds on this week's deliverables, so you can see exactly where the extra work goes. 2) Share that count with your heaviest client once, so the conversation is based on facts. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every deliverable tracked with rounds counted against the agreement, and clients reminded about approvals. Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
